steps.body: Composing and decomposing together let you build new shapes from old ones, then take them apart again — the pieces are never lost.
steps.narration: Composing and decomposing together let you build new shapes from old ones, then take them apart again — the pieces are never lost.

widget.prompt: Two triangles are joined, then that shape is joined to another like it. Tap what the four triangles make.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: Four triangles make a larger four-sided shape, not a three-sided one.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: Straight-edged pieces always leave straight edges.

hotspots.label: cube
hotspots.feedback: A cube is solid; joining flat pieces keeps the result flat.

widget.missFeedback: Build it in stages: two triangles make a square, and two squares make a rectangle.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — two squares' worth of triangles line up into a rectangle.

predict.prompt: You build a new shape from old pieces. How do you decide what to call it?
predict.reveal: A shape is named by its own defining attributes, not by what it was built from.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s compose new.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

explanationVariants: Name the result by its own outline.

widget.prompt: Two squares are pushed together side by side to make a rectangle. How many sides does a rectangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the sides of both starting pieces; joining them hides the edges that meet inside.
That misses one sides of the finished rectangle; count all the way around the outside.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

widget.prompt: What new shape do six triangles make when joined?

options.label: A hexagon
options.feedback: Correct — joining six triangles makes a hexagon because they meet at a single centre point.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Straight-sided pieces cannot join into a circle; every edge they contribute stays straight.

options.label: A cone
options.feedback: That is a solid, but joining flat pieces edge to edge keeps the result flat.

options.label: Nothing — shapes cannot be joined
options.feedback: Shapes combine readily; a new, larger shape is exactly what composing produces.

explanationVariants: Any build can be taken apart.

widget.prompt: How can a hexagon be taken apart?

options.label: Into six triangles
options.feedback: Correct — cut from the centre to each corner and the hexagon separates into six triangles.

options.label: Into nothing — it is one piece
options.feedback: Any shape can be cut into smaller shapes; being one piece now does not prevent it.

options.label: Into a circle
options.feedback: Straight cuts produce straight edges, so a round piece cannot appear.

options.label: Into a cube
options.feedback: A cube is a solid; cutting a flat shape leaves flat pieces.

explanationVariants: Not the pieces it came from.

widget.prompt: What makes a shape a square?

options.label: Having 4 straight sides
options.feedback: Correct — the number of straight sides is what makes a shape a square, whatever it looks like otherwise.

options.label: Being red
options.feedback: Color can change freely without the shape changing; it is not a defining attribute.

options.label: Being large
options.feedback: Size can change freely without the shape changing; a tiny square is still a square.

options.label: Pointing upward
options.feedback: Turning a shape does not change what it is; orientation is not a defining attribute.
